summary: John sees new heaven and new earth, first heaven and earth passed, sea no more, New Jerusalem coming down from heaven like bride adorned, voice says God will dwell with people, will wipe every tear, death no more, mourning crying pain no more. Alpha and Omega makes all things new. City measured with jasper, gold like clear glass, twelve foundations with twelve apostles, gates twelve tribes, no temple — Lord God Almighty and Lamb are temple, no need sun — glory illumines.
whyItMatters: Climax of Bible — not escape to heaven but heaven coming down, God dwelling with people, tears wiped, as Eden restored and more. Answers longing for home, end of death, and what forever looks like: not boring clouds but city, culture, presence.

context.author: John on Patmos
context.audience: Seven churches in Roman Asia, under imperial pressure (the scale of Domitianic persecution is debated among historians)
context.date: Most scholars date Revelation c. AD 90–95 under Domitian; a minority argues for a Nero-era date (c. AD 65–68)
context.literaryForm: Apocalypse — symbolic visions with Old Testament imagery

outline.heading: New heaven and new earth, sea no more, New Jerusalem as bride descends
God dwells with people, wipes tears, death no more
City measured — jasper, gold, pearls, huge cube
No temple or need for sun — Lord and Lamb are temple and lamp

keyVerses.text: I heard a loud voice out of heaven saying, “Behold, God’s dwelling is with people; and he will dwell with them, and they will be his people, and God himself will be with them as their God. He will wipe away every tear from their eyes. Death will be no more; neither will there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain any more. The first things have passed away.”
keyVerses.why: Center promise — dwelling with, tears wiped, death no more.

keyVerses.text: He who sits on the throne said, “Behold, I am making all things new.” He said, “Write, for these words of God are faithful and true.”
keyVerses.why: Not all new things but all things new — renewal not replacement.

keyVerses.text: I saw no temple in it, for the Lord God the Almighty and the Lamb are its temple. The city has no need for the sun or moon to shine, for the very glory of God illuminated it and its lamp is the Lamb.
keyVerses.why: No temple and no need for sun or moon — presence itself is temple and light.

themes: no temple; no need for sun or moon; Lamb is light

questions.question: What does 'new heaven and new earth, first passed away, sea no more' mean?
questions.answer: Not annihilation of planet but renewal — first passed, Greek aperchomai — passed away like old garment. Sea in Revelation is source of beast, chaos, separation — no more sea means no more chaos, evil, separation. New heaven and earth = heavens and earth reunited, as in Lord's Prayer 'on earth as in heaven.' Making all things new, not all new things.

questions.question: Why New Jerusalem as bride adorned for husband? Why city as bride?
questions.answer: Bride image used earlier: church as bride of Christ, prepared. City is not building but people — community. Bride adorned = prepared, beautiful, ready. Coming down from heaven = gift descending, not humans building up to heaven. Contrast with Babel trying to build up to heaven; this comes down.

questions.question: What does 'God will wipe every tear, death no more, mourning crying pain no more' mean literally?
questions.answer: Most quoted comfort verses, often at funerals. Promise is eschatological: former things — death, mourning, crying, pain — belong to old order that passes. Wipe tears suggests God tenderly, personally removing. Not that tears never happened, but that they are followed by comfort and absence of cause. Death last enemy destroyed (1 Cor 15:26).

questions.question: What is inside cowardly, unbelieving, etc. will have part in second death? Is that contradictory to hope?
questions.answer: Verse 8 list — cowardly, faithless, detestable, murderers, sexually immoral, sorcerers, idolaters, liars — their part in lake of fire second death. Jarring after universal hope, but apocalyptic honesty: choices have consequence, evil not ignored. Second death is final separation, contrast to life in city where nothing unclean enters (v27). List mirrors vice lists elsewhere, warning.

questions.question: Why describe city with measurements, jasper, gold clear as glass, 12 foundations, gates?
questions.answer: Measurements are symbolic: 12,000 stadia (~1,400 miles) cube — huge, equal length width height — like Holy of Holies cube expanded to city size — whole city is Holy of Holies where God dwells. Twelve gates twelve tribes, twelve foundations twelve apostles — includes old and new people of God. Jasper, gold transparent, pearls — beauty, wealth, purity, but also shows no need for temple economy — city's wealth is presence.

questions.question: Why no temple and no need sun or moon in city?
questions.answer: In old Jerusalem, temple was place of presence, sun/moon marked time. Here, Lord God Almighty and Lamb are temple — presence everywhere, not confined. Glory illumines, Lamb lamp — no need sun. Means no mediation needed, no darkness, no night cycles. Fulfillment of Isaiah 60:19-20.

glossary.def: Not rebuilt Middle Eastern city but symbol of renewed people and place where heaven and earth overlap.
Old order passing, not annihilation — renewal language.
Final separation/judgment after physical death, contrast to life in New Jerusalem.
